# EvToggle

> A toggle is a two-state button that switches an option on or off. Use it standalone, or grouped in a ToggleGroup for a set of related single- or multi-select options.

| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:toggle` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvToggle } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvToggle>` or `<ev-toggle>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/toggle/EvToggle.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<button class="ev-toggle">` |
| Used inside | `evoq-ui:toggle-group` (EvToggleGroup) |

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Toggle**, frame `4518:85699` (Toggle). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use a single Toggle for an on/off state tied to one option (bold, mute). Use a ToggleGroup for a related set — single-select like a view switcher, or multi-select like text formatting.

### When not to use

- Don't use for a binary setting in a form — use a Switch (`evoq-ui:switch`). Don't use for mutually exclusive options that need labels and descriptions — use radio buttons (`evoq-ui:radio-group`).

### Do

- Use a clear icon or short label so the toggled option is obvious. Keep the active state visually distinct. Use a consistent Variant and Size across a group.

### Don't

- Don't mix Default and Outline variants within one group. Don't rely on color alone to show the active state — pair it with the filled background and label weight.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvToggle`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<button class="ev-toggle">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:toggle` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
